title: Vandal Kingdom
capsule: The Vandal Kingdom (435–534) was founded in North Africa by Gaiseric after the Vandals and Alans crossed from Spain and seized the Roman diocese of Africa, initially settling under the Treaty of 435 and then capturing Carthage in October 439. Under Gaiseric (r. 428–477) the kingdom became a Mediterranean naval power, seizing Sardinia, Corsica, the Balearics, and sacking Rome in 455. His successors maintained Arian Christianity against Catholic North African populations, producing protracted religious conflicts. In 533 Emperor Justinian dispatched Belisarius, who defeated King Gelimer at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum; Gelimer surrendered in 534 and was paraded at a Constantinople triumph, ending the kingdom and reincorporating Africa into the Eastern Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core North African territory is well established from Roman-era sources and archaeology; the island dependencies (Sardinia, Corsica, Balearics) appear in sources but the extent of actual administrative control on those islands is debated.
